recentItems.title: Macron and Carney to hold talks on strengthening Canada-France economic and defense ties
recentItems.description:
(20 Sep 2026) 
RESTRICTION SUMMARY:

++STARTS AND ENDS ON SOUNDBITE++

AP VIA AGENCY POOL (AFPTV) 
Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, France - 20 September 2026
++STARTS ON SOUNDBITE++
1. SOUNDBITE (French) Emmanuel Macron, French President:
"For the first time in our history, we will have an official visit from a Canadian Prime Minister tomorrow at noon, and it is also an important moment that we have planned with Prime Minister (Mark) Carney. This will first allow us to improve the prospects for cooperation between Canada and Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon and, more broadly, to work on and strengthen our bilateral economic relations as well as our defense relations, giving even greater substance to the strategic autonomy we share. You know how much Canada is getting closer to Europe, and if I may say so, this alliance is taking on a northern dimension by being here on this soil and being able to make it a reality. It was obviously included."
++BLACK FRAMES++
2. SOUNDBITE (French) Emmanuel Macron, French President:
“I came to this part of the world where we have close friends, including Canada. I extended this invitation to him, and the Prime Minister responded, which I find to be a very strong gesture of friendship, just a few days after he expressed his desire to work more closely with the European Union, giving it a very concrete dimension. So here we are, France is present thanks to Saint Pierre and Miquelon, through Saint Pierre and Miquelon, here at the heart of global issues in this region and this also connects us with Canada, and it will be a way to talk about the future together and to strengthen our relations in many areas."
++BLACK FRAMES++
3. SOUNDBITE (French) Emmanuel Macron, French President:
"Canada is a country with significant resources of critical minerals and rare earths, so these are things we want to contract with, France as well as the European Union, and which is also (Canada), as you know, a major producer of fossil hydrocarbons and it produces gas which, through its production and also through what they do in refining, helps balance the global market and so, there have been agreements, what we call swap agreements, exchanges that have been made by several countries in Europe and so what we want to do is not just look, but consolidate and conclude agreements to clearly have more liquefied gas that can go to the Atlantic coast. Because today there is a lot that goes to the Pacific coast, so allowing them diversification. But what we are doing, what we have done in recent days and weeks, is very concrete. That is to say, we are fighting to secure supply agreements in the coming months because we want to be prepared for everything and we want to protect the French people and be well-prepared in terms of gas, diesel, jet fuel, to ensure we do not run out (of it).”
++BLACK FRAMES++
4. SOUNDBITE (French) Emmanuel Macron, French President:
++ENDS ON SOUNDBITE++
STORYLINE:
French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney are set to meet Sunday to deepen economic and security ties on the remote North Atlantic archipelago of Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon.

The meeting comes days after Carney embraced the prospect of Canada becoming the European Union’s first associate member, saying closer ties with the continent would ensure no country could control Canada’s markets or undermine its sovereignty.

U.S. President Donald Trump’s tariffs, demands for economic concessions and repeated talk of making Canada the 51st state have pushed Ottawa to reduce its dependence on its neighbor and pursue deeper economic, security and political relationships with Europe.

ASSOCIATED PRESS
Schwerin, Germany - 20 September 2026
1. SOUNDBITE (English) Kerstin Sopke, The Associated Press:
"Today voters are casting ballots here in the eastern state of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and in the capital Berlin. Both election could deliver further gains for the far-right party AfD and increase pressure on Chancellor Friedrich Merz.
Merz’s authority was badly damaged by his party’s defeat two weeks ago in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt. The anti-migration, Russia-friendly Alternative for Germany finished just short of a majority there.
The AfD is expected to make gains in both elections today, although its path to power remains blocked because major parties have ruled out working with it.
Merz’s center-right CDU is facing a difficult night. In Berlin, the party risks losing the mayor’s office, while in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania it could fall below the 5% threshold needed to enter the state parliament.
Poor results in both states could intensify pressure on chancellor Merz’s leadership and raise new questions about the stability of Germany’s national government."
2. Mid of person casting vote 
3. Wide of woman inside polling station
4. Person casting vote 
5. Close of person casting vote 
6. Interior of polling station 
STORYLINE:
Polling stations opened Sunday in two German state elections in which the far-right AfD party is expected to make further gains that could determine whether Chancellor Friedrich Merz can hold on to power and push ahead with reforms in Europe’s biggest economy.

The state elections are taking place in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, a largely rural region in the formerly communist and less prosperous east, and in the capital, Berlin.

The vote comes two weeks after the anti-migration, Russia-friendly Alternative for Germany, or AfD, finished just short of a majority in the small eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, and has its best chance yet of forming the country’s first far-right regional government since World War II.

Merz’s authority was severely damaged by his party’s stinging defeat in the Sept. 6 election by AfD — a result that shocked many Germans who had believed their country had developed an immunity to nationalism and assertions of racial superiority after confronting the horrors of its Nazi past through education and laws to outlaw persecution.

The AfD is expected to make significant gains in Sunday's elections as well, but has no realistic path to power in Berlin and faces a much stronger challenge from Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania’s center-left governor than it did from Merz’s party in Saxony-Anhalt. 

Prospects for Merz’s center-right Christian Democratic Union are bleaker. It could lose the mayor’s office in Berlin. If things go very badly, it could fail for the first time to win seats in a state legislature anywhere by falling below 5% of the vote in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, where it was already weak.

Merz, 70, became Germany’s leader 16 months ago with promises to turn around an economy that has barely grown in years, but has failed to lift a sullen national mood and has himself become deeply unpopular.

The strong showing of AfD in the Saxony-Anhalt election has further weakened the chancellor's standing on the national level as well, and in the past two weeks there have been calls even from within his own party to replace him as chancellor. No top-level allies have called publicly for his departure, and many have warned against “personnel debates.” 

AP video by: Pietro De Cristofaro

recentItems.title: Charlize Theron hosts block party in support of South Africa
recentItems.description:
(20 Sep 2026) 
ASSOCIATED PRESS 
Los Angeles - 19 September 2026
1. Medium Charlize Theron poses 
2. SOUNDBITE (English) Charlize Theron, actor

“I would say I'm most proud of the community that we've created and that's really a celebration that is part of tonight. It's the celebration of a lot of people here who've stuck with us for 20 years. That community, the work that we do, or our partners on the ground do in South Africa, is impossible without this community here. And so I'm proud of the longevity that we've had with that.”
3. Medium Charlize Theron gives interview 
4. SOUNDBITE (English) Charlize Theron, actor
“Listen, it's unfortunate that we're living in a time where femicide is very real.  And we're living in a time where funding globally has been none to zero. And if it wasn't for us coming together, people will be left in the dark. People will die, people are dying. So I don't need a lot of explanation around why it's important to understand that. Some of us are lucky. It's a roll of the dice where you're born and the life that you're gonna have. And some of us get really lucky with that. I think understanding that and making sure that you make sure that your neighbor is OK, that's a good thing.”
5. Close up Charlize Theron gives interview
6.  SOUNDBITE (English) Charlize Theron, actor
“The worst thing a mom can do is try to put something on them. I have teenagers. It's almost a reverse psychology. I almost have to go the other way around. But I try to live my life in a way as an example so that at least they can see what that looks like. I demand, as a mom, awareness. I want my children to be aware outside of their bubble. And so that's the only thing right now that I kind of like have made part of our values. Like what's going on in the world and how does that pertain to you? And how is the world different from this life that you're having here? Those things to me are really important. And wherever they find their philanthropy, wherever they want to end up, that's on them.”
7. Wide Charlize Theron dances on stage 


AP VIDEO: Sarah Jones-Smith 
PRODUCTION: Sarah Jones-Smith
STORYLINE:
Charlize Theron hosted her Africa Outreach Project 2026 Block Party in Los Angles on Saturday. 

The Oscar-winning actor provides funding, builds community, and amplifies the voices of young people in Southern Africa through her CTAOP foundation. 


“If it wasn't for us coming together, people will be left in the dark. People will die, people are dying. So I don't need a lot of explanation around why it's important to understand that,” Theron said.

Theron also said, while she does not place expectations on her children to continue this effort, she emphasizes the importance of awareness. 

“I demand, as a mom, awareness. I want my children to be aware outside of their bubble. And so that's the only thing right now that I kind of like have made part of our values.”

STORYLINE:
A-listers from Mark Hamill and Samuel L Jackson, to Francis Ford Coppola and Spike Lee flocked to join George Lucas and Mellody Hobson at the long-awaited opening night of the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art.

Others posing for photos on the red carpet, Saturday, included Ron Howard and daughter Bryce Dallas Howard, Justin Trudeau and Katy Perry, Oprah Winfrey, Cynthia Erivo, Jon M. Chu, Greta Gerwig, Guillermo del Toro, Pharrell Williams, Laura Dern, Kim Kardashian, Camila Cabello, Nicolas Cage, Tyler Perry, Michael B Jordan and co-chair of the opening night Lewis Hamilton.

Co-founded by Lucas and his wife, Mellody Hobson, the museum brings together works of art from around the world, including pieces from Lucas’ personal collection and objects connected to his career in filmmaking.

The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art is sited near Lucas' alma mater, the University of Southern California
